outputs.purpose: The pack itself — the index, the workpaper per control, and the sampling worksheets — for a human to hand to an auditor. It is not the manifest: the manifest carries the claims and is what `:push` is bound to, while the pack is the deliverable those claims were assembled into. Pushing a rendered pack into Noru would duplicate a register Noru already keeps, so the pack stays local and only the tested conclusion per control lands.

exit_codes.0: manifest is valid; warnings may be present
exit_codes.1: manifest has validation errors, including a conclusion already expired at --as-of
exit_codes.2: usage error, unreadable file, or unparseable YAML

invalid.expect_message: before the window it covers had ended
is not in the queue snapshot
was not digested by this scan
deferred exception is one nobody has dealt with

collapses_to.tool: a single idempotency-keyed ingest for an assurance conclusion — the control, the period it covers, what was inspected, the sample that was drawn and the conclusion with its validity — so the piece would state the conclusion once rather than render it into an evidence body and probe for its own marker. The gap is not really call count here: it is that a tested conclusion about a control over a period has no first-class shape in the published API, so it has to travel as evidence text

idempotency.verified_at: The createEvidence tool description published by https://api.noru.tech/v1/mcp documents creating text/note/link evidence with optional control mappings and states that file uploads are not supported over MCP; it documents no idempotency key. The "Idempotency/Upsert Behavior" section of https://api.noru.tech/llms.txt covers `POST /v1/assets` and `POST /v1/security-findings` only, so nothing published covers evidence.
idempotency.gap: No idempotency key is documented for evidence, so this piece does not rely on one: it embeds a marker built from the pack key, the workpaper key and a digest of the rendered workpaper in the evidence description, and probes getOrganizationEvidence before creating. A documented key would let the probe go away and would make a re-tested control an update rather than a second record.

idempotency.verified_at: The linkEvidenceToControl tool description published by https://api.noru.tech/v1/mcp documents linking an evidence record to a control and optionally narrowing the link to specific evidence-item template ids. Whether linking the same pair twice is a no-op is not documented anywhere public, so the piece does not assume it.
idempotency.gap: Nothing published says what a repeated link does, so this operation is only planned when the state snapshot shows the record exists and the control link does not. A documented key, or a documented no-op on a repeated link, would remove the need to read the organization's evidence links first.

source.note: Which frameworks the organization is actually being audited against. A pack is about one of them, and the id comes from here rather than from an argument somebody typed.
The controls in the framework's scope, with their status. Ids come from Noru; this plugin ships none.

The full context for one control: what the framework expects, what is already linked, coverage, and whether a testing procedure is available. The procedure text is deliberately not stored — the pack records that one exists and the tester writes what they actually did.
Every evidence record linked to a control with its status and expiry. A record that expired during the window is the difference between a control that was covered and one that looks covered today.
The catalogue of framework-level evidence-item templates, used to resolve titles and types for expectations the control context returns by id.

exit_codes.1: drift, validation failure, an expired conclusion under --as-of, missing prerequisite input, or a stale plan
exit_codes.2: usage error, including a push without --confirm
